This week the world's map moved because of water, fire and inventory.

Two oil chokepoints contested at once. A strike on the Caspian that welded two wars together. 420 sq km of France gone in four days.

5 ways the map moved — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The US paused strikes on Iran for a third day. NYT and the Guardian report officials advised the halt over dwindling interceptor stocks. Trump says talks are on; Iran denies direct talks. Qatar and Pakistan mediating.

The limit is a supply chain, not a border.

2/ With Hormuz shut, the Houthis turned on Saudi oil in the Red Sea. Yemen's recognised govt told Al Jazeera they "want to copy Iran's Hormuz control."

The Guardian: Suez is now the only fully open route for Gulf oil. Japan, S. Korea and the Philippines are scrambling.

3/ Ukraine struck an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea — 1,500 km from its front line (BBC).

Tehran's FM says it "cannot go unanswered." Kyiv shrugged.

Two wars, now physically linked. Zelenskyy and Netanyahu are both in Washington this week.

4/ One blaze near Bordeaux burned 420+ sq km in under four days (BBC). The Madrid region is seeing its worst fires on record, with flames a short drive from the capital and 200+ homes gone (NYT).

A fresh heatwave is arriving. The land-cover map of two countries just changed.

5/ ~500 people are believed dead in shipwrecks off Myanmar (Guardian). Malaysia detained 100+ Rohingya who had gone to the UN for help (Al Jazeera).

The 1951 Refugee Convention turns 75 this week.

The Andaman Sea is a route because the land borders around it are shut.

The data behind it: only 8 countries send more than a million refugees abroad — Afghanistan, Syria, Sudan, South Sudan, DR Congo, Venezuela, Ukraine, Myanmar.

Myanmar's dark stripe is why boats keep leaving Rakhine.
